correctness.rationale: For a dissociation set with a=|S cap X|, b=|S cap Y|, mixed degree constraints require a,b<=2 when m,n>=3. Cases (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2) contribute mn, t(m-1),t(n-1),binom(t,2). Pure shore parts give (1+z)^m+(1+z)^n-1, hence exact D. Inclusion-maximal mixed pairs require both unmatched indices: (m-t)(n-t); triples require matched/unmatched other-side pair: t(m+n-2t); all matched two-pair 4-sets are maximal, and whole shores are maximal. Thus M formula. Only all-matched equal shores r=4 have a single maximal size: G444 is Q3; for crowns r>=5 min 4 max r. Independent all-subset enumeration of five (m,n,t) triples, including K33, crown r=3, cube, and mixed unequal shores, matched both polynomials exactly.
residual_risks: m,n>=3 and forbidden edges must be a matching; not arbitrary deleted bipartite subgraphs.

value.rationale: Matching-deleted bicliques/crown graphs are a natural family interpolating complete bipartite and regular complements. Exact polynomials distinguish all and inclusion-maximal dissociation sets, classify the unique equal-size maximal case, and exhibit unbounded maximal/minimal spread in connected regular bipartite graphs. These are exact, structurally motivated invariants, not an arbitrary finite slice.
